kind: agent network/framework plus native-CLI workspace adapters

runtime.execution: asyncio SDK event network and bounded model/tool loop; separate per-channel native CLI subprocess adapters
runtime.service_boundary: SDK owns network/mod/membership/project/cache fabric; individual workers/adapters consume it and native/provider services

summary: Networked Python workers communicate through direct/channel events and configured tools; workspace adapters separately launch external coding CLIs. Several prototype/logging contracts are materially weaker than their names suggest.

inspection.scope: Selected source excerpts trace exposed entry/loop/request/action/result/state boundaries and relevant capability mechanisms; listed tests are read as source only.
inspection.limits: No acquired code executed, dependencies installed or live providers invoked. Claims concern this pinned snapshot; untraced catalog tools and dependency internals are not inferred.

actions.name: WorkerAgent.react / @on
actions.lifecycle: matched handlers awaited before configured model trigger
actions.authority: Python author config; exposed tools determine model authority

actions.name: AgentRunner.run_agent / run_llm / finish
actions.input: context, instruction, iteration bound, selected tools; finish reason
actions.output: action trajectory, tool values/error strings, completion
actions.lifecycle: serial awaited tools and model calls until finish/direct answer/bound
actions.authority: configured model invokes installed tools without a per-call approval gate in this loop

actions.name: update_tools / configured Python tools / MCP
actions.input: mod adapter tools, MCP config, module/function tool config
actions.output: current tool list; import failures logged/omitted
actions.lifecycle: snapshot refreshed explicitly; ongoing orchestration retains selected list

actions.name: send_direct_message / send_channel_message / reply_channel_message
actions.output: EventResponse and message IDs; notifications with original ID
actions.lifecycle: network routing then in-memory recipient queue; not model-read receipt
actions.authority: connected agent; workspace/channel membership and secret boundary

actions.name: retrieve_channel_messages / retrieve_direct_messages / list_channels
actions.output: message/history dictionaries or empty timeout fallback
actions.lifecycle: awaited response; Worker history requests keyed by channel/peer

actions.name: react_to_message / upload_file / get_agent_list
actions.output: EventResponse, file UUID or agent IDs
actions.lifecycle: awaited workspace calls; local/native file access depends on adapter
actions.authority: configured worker; not universal tool exposure

actions.name: start_project / stop_project / complete_project / get_project / send_project_message
actions.input: template ID, goal, collaborators; project ID/status/content
actions.output: project IDs/status/messages; template tools optionally final results
actions.lifecycle: creation response; optional polling until terminal status/time limit
actions.authority: model configured with project adapter; project permission checked on state operations

actions.name: set_project_global_state / get_project_global_state / create_cache
actions.lifecycle: remote mod state; cache correlated response wait ten seconds
actions.authority: authorized project member or configured shared-cache consumer

actions.name: schedule_task
actions.lifecycle: resident delayed task; cancelled on teardown without await

actions.name: AgentNetwork.process_event / subscribe / poll_events
actions.lifecycle: in-memory fanout/dedup; poll drains before receiver processes
actions.authority: fabric owns transport/membership/secret verification; internal mods trusted

actions.name: load_mod / unload_mod / restart
actions.input: Python mod path/config or new NetworkConfig
actions.lifecycle: immediate shared mutation; restart shuts whole network; ID-only unload mismatch
actions.authority: network administrator/system-event surface; no turn-bound activation fence

actions.name: Claude workspace adapter set_mode / stop
actions.lifecycle: mode changes next CLI command; stop terminates active groups and drops queues
actions.authority: workspace controller; execute passes native permission bypass

actions.name: LLMCallLogger.log_call / LLMLogReader.get_logs
actions.lifecycle: standalone append/rotation; main EventBased logger does not call it
actions.authority: Python consumer must wire it; logging failure does not prevent work

filesystem.detail: External Claude adapter exposes local Read/Write/Edit/Bash and uploads; SDK core instead supplies workspace/cache file APIs and configured custom tools. Direct text adapter has no tool loop.

processes.detail: Workspace Claude adapter owns external CLI process groups, streams output and has escalating stop; SDK model executor only awaits supplied tool implementations.

code_actions.detail: Python event handlers and configured function tools can compose programs; traced model turn dispatches named JSON tools rather than model-authored general code cells.

persistent_kernel.detail: No model-addressable persistent Python execution kernel established in SDK orchestrator, messaging mods or workspace adapters inspected.

standing_database.detail: Remote project/global state and shared cache are supporting shared data services; no arbitrary standing SQL table/query API established in traced adapters.

workflow_programming.detail: Worker event triggers/custom handlers, Python coroutine scheduling, mod/MCP tools and generated project-template tools form exposed orchestration surfaces.

multi_model.detail: Each configured AgentRunner resolves its own model/provider before orchestration; network peers may differ. Native workspace adapters separately use external CLIs.

live_collaboration.detail: SDK agent direct/channel/group/broadcast messages and threaded replies carry shared-room notifications into event-triggered model reactions. Delivery receipts only prove routing/queue activity, sometimes even less.

concurrent_work.detail: Workspace adapter serializes each channel and runs channels concurrently; SDK schedules resident tasks and multiple network participants. SDK tools within one turn are serial.

steering_interrupt.detail: Workspace control can change mode and stop all current channel processes, losing queued messages; base shutdown gathers workers instead of cancelling them. No universal model/tool quiescence guarantee.

turn_redefinition.detail: Python react override, templates/tool snapshots and mod pipeline are programmable building blocks. ONM staged guard/transform/observe pipeline is separate prototype, not this SDK loop.

compaction.detail: Claude adapter relays native compaction notices and infers compaction from quiet output; direct adapter simply drops oldest shared history. No managed cross-path compaction choices.

context_repair.detail: History retrieval, project state and native per-channel resume IDs can retrieve context; no repair/versioned projection operation preserving authoritative originals traced.

original_audit.detail: Main SDK model logger is effectively no-op; message snapshots/archives overwrite, batch and expire. Separate JSONL logger can persist selected calls but neither guarantees complete original I/O retention.

audit_query.detail: Standalone LLMLogReader filters file-backed selected calls, and messaging history is queryable. They cannot query unrecorded main-loop calls or prove complete causal history.

hot_change.detail: Tools refresh explicitly; live network mod load/unload and immediate adapter mode changes exist. No affected-turn/workflow activation fence; ID-only mod unload can leave instance reachable.

rebuild_continuity.detail: External CLI session IDs resume channels; network restart shuts fabric and may continue after mod-load errors. No outpost transfer, request drain, reversible compile/refit or guaranteed child quiescence.

remote_services.detail: Agents consume authenticated event network and remote workspace/project/cache; SDK AgentNetwork is itself the fabric governor, distinct from Arconaut consumer role.

self_improvement.detail: Custom Python tools, module loading and external Bash/write permit editing/extensions; no model-governed experiment/recovery/adoption policy or executable continuity loop traced.

complaints.detail: No dedicated state-capturing model frustration/complaint record with separately tracked repair obligation established in studied SDK/adapters/project/messaging paths.

authority.detail: SDK configured tools execute directly. External Claude execute mode bypasses approvals; plan restricts native/MCP set. Normal transport uses agent secrets but broad no-secret system-event exemption requires separate authorization review.

evaluation.detail: Read tests cover mock worker message forwarding, actual temporary file logger/storage and separate ONM ordering. They do not validate durable logging of wired loop, live CLI termination or cross-channel direct-history isolation.

time_order.detail: Gateway overwrites timestamps with current seconds, dedup marks before processing and polling drains queues. Message IDs/future keys are not durable receiver acknowledgments or crash-safe causal ordering.

evidence.claim: Configured event triggers or react-to-all invoke AgentRunner.run_agent; not every incoming event starts a model turn.
Custom matched handlers run before collaborator reaction; handler exceptions log; teardown cancels scheduled tasks without awaiting their termination.
update_tools snapshots mod/MCP/configured Python tools; custom import failures degrade to an empty set and restore sys.path.
run_agent passes selected mod/MCP/custom tools and current configuration/context into orchestrate_agent.
Each orchestration builds templated system/user context; default maximum is ten iterations; awaits provider completion and attempted event-based logging.
Model tools execute serially by name and parsed JSON arguments; finish ends chain, results/errors append to conversation, and model interaction failure ends trajectory.
Wired EventBasedLLMLogger constructs an entry then debug-logs and returns UUID only: no file write or network event occurs.
Separate LLMCallLogger rotates at size threshold and deletes old files by configured retention; it is not the logger used in orchestrate_agent.
Standalone logger appends JSONL; errors are logged rather than propagated, with no fsync contract.
Standalone file reader supports model/since/error/search and pagination, skips malformed records; it cannot recover records never written by the main loop.
SDK timestamps are overwritten with current seconds; IDs enter dedup set before mod processing; first mod response intercepts, otherwise delivery reports success.
Channel/group/broadcast and direct routes enqueue subscribed recipients; missing recipient queue skips; polling drains in-memory queues without processing acknowledgments.
Live SDK uses ordered first-intercept mods, target-mod routing and shallow copied event; exceptions in ordinary pipeline log and continue.
ONM envelope is explicitly separate from existing SDK Event; guard/transform/observer prototype is not the traced network path.
Separate prototype sorts guard/transform/observer stages and exposes mutable mod registration; unit support does not establish agent availability.
Runtime load_mod imports Python, binds/initializes then mutates mod registry and live processor dictionary; no turn/workflow fence or fresh-code reload.
unload checks dynamic ID but retrieves instance by supplied path; ID-only call can unregister without finding/removing path-keyed running mod.
Network restart owns network shutdown/config/module reset and continues even if module loading fails; not consumer-only executable refit.
Transport authenticates normal events by agent secret, but no-secret system events except polling/unregister bypass this gate; internal mods bypass authentication.
Worker API sends direct/channel messages and replies/reactions via workspace connection, returning event responses.
History futures keyed only by channel/peer wait ten seconds; timeout/errors return empty-history shape, and concurrent same-channel requests can overwrite future.
schedule_task creates tracked asyncio sleep-then-coro task and returns Task handle, not persistent external scheduling.
Native tool schemas bind send_direct_message, send_channel_message, reply_channel_message, list_channels and retrieve history to adapter methods; threading limit and pagination are explicit.
Unknown channel is created with all active agents; channel notifications carry original_event_id but per-recipient route errors are logged, not propagated as failed delivery.
Message history is mutable ID-keyed dictionary; cleanup/dumping run on insert and main snapshot saves every configured batch, independent of route success.
Main message_history.json overwrites nonatomically; serialization/load/write errors log and may yield partial or empty history.
Daily gzip archives merge IDs and overwrite; corrupt existing archive may be replaced after logged parse failure; archive errors log and retention deletes old data.
Tools expose list/start/stop/complete/get_project and project messaging with goal/template/collaborator IDs.
Generic start returns creation response; generated template tools can wait by two-second polling for terminal project status with 300-second default limit.
Project state get/set checks project permission, then mutates state and returns prior/current values; not an exposed SQL database or persistent computation kernel.
Shared cache value/mime/group API sends event, waits up to ten seconds for correlated completion and returns cache ID or None.
Adapter marks cursor/processed IDs before dispatch, serializes per-channel work in memory and runs separate channels concurrently; finally gathers active tasks rather than cancelling them.
Control set_mode immediately changes plan/execute; other actions delegate; cursor advances before action and exceptions are swallowed.
Plan permits read-oriented tools with Claude plan mode; execute requests permission bypass plus Bash/write and workspace MCP; configuration is fixed for each launched CLI process.
Stop affects all running channel processes, escalates group termination, discards pending channel messages and posts status; it does not pause shared services.
External Claude CLI launches per channel with stdout/stderr pipes and POSIX process group; fifteen-second quiet intervals are labeled compaction without proving actual compaction.
Result session IDs persist channel resume map; system compaction notices surface; process wait followed by final text and temporary MCP cleanup, while most native outputs remain external CLI-owned.
Direct adapter truncates shared conversation list and sends streaming chat-completion payload without tool schemas; same history is shared by concurrent channels.
Each orchestration resolves auto/environment or configured provider/model credentials and constructs its model provider.

tests.focus: Worker direct send and EventResponse forwarding
tests.oracle: MockWorkerAgent skips parent initialization and uses AsyncMock workspace send; asserts exact arguments/response fields, not real network delivery.

tests.focus: Bounded in-memory messages and dump retention
tests.oracle: Temporary storage helper receives synthetic timestamps; count limit asserted; archive assertion conditional on directory existence, so not a fail-closed archival oracle.
Synthetic guard/transform/observer implementations assert stage order and rejection; not the SDK gateway processor or network integration.
Real temporary JSONL file existence and values are asserted; tested class differs from wired EventBasedLLMLogger, leaving no-op integration uncovered.

strengths: Actual event-triggered peer rooms with tool-backed messaging and project-state APIs.
Python handlers/mods and externally launched agents supply distinct extension levels.
Explicit plan/execute native tool set and process-group stop surface.
limits: Wired model logger does not persist/send; standalone logger tests do not cover it.
ONM staged pipeline is future-envelope prototype; live SDK first-intercept mod processor has different semantics.
Adapter cursor advances before dispatch and direct adapter shares history across concurrent channels.
Network mutation/restart governs shared fabric and lacks turn fence/refit guarantees.
arconaut_questions: What receipt distinguishes routed, queued, started, model-consumed and persisted messages?
How should shared provider-history isolation and audit integration be tested across concurrent channels?
Can model-configurable extension activation be fenced at affected turn/workflow boundaries while fabric remains independently managed?
